answer: A verifiable random lottery admits only a fixed number of new identities per epoch, so entry is rationed by time rather than money. A farm of n identities must queue for roughly n divided by the quota epochs, and each waiting epoch is a cost that grows with the farm while an honest agent waits once. Like a sonnet with its strict lines, or layers of shale stacked slowly in an orchard soil, admission is built up one rationed layer at a time.
